p1.original: Political Power from a Cotton Monopoly
p1.zh: 来自棉花垄断的政治力量

p3.original: Many of the opening case studies have focused on current events. This one steps into the past to observe how monopoly, or near monopolies, have helped shape history. In spring 1773, the East India Company, a firm that, in its time, was designated “too big to fail,” was experiencing financial difficulties. To help shore up the failing firm, the British Parliament authorized the Tea Act. The act continued the tax on teas and made the East India Company the sole legal supplier of tea to the American colonies. By November, the citizens of Boston had had enough. They refused to permit the unloading of tea, citing their main complaint: “No taxation without representation.” Several newspapers, including The Massachusetts Gazette, warned arriving tea-bearing ships, “We are prepared, and shall not fail to pay them an unwelcome visit by The Mohawks.”
p3.zh: 许多开始的案例研究都侧重于时事。 这一步步走进过去,来观察垄断或接近垄断是如何帮助塑造历史的。1773年春,东印度公司在当时被定为“太大不能失败”的一家公司正面临财政困难。 为了帮助支撑倒闭的公司,英国议会批准了"茶法".该法案延续了茶叶税制,使东印度公司成为美国殖民地唯一合法的茶叶供应商.到了11月,波士顿市民已经受够了. 他们拒绝允许卸下茶叶,他们主要抱怨说 : “ 没有代表就没有税。 ”包括《马萨诸塞公报》在内的多家报纸警告前来的含茶船说 , “ 我们准备好了,而且莫霍克人不会不欢迎他们访问。 ”

p4.original: Step forward in time to 1860—the eve of the American Civil War—to another near monopoly supplier of historical significance: the U.S. cotton industry. At that time, the Southern states provided the majority of the cotton Britain imported. The South, wanting to secede from the Union, hoped to leverage Britain’s high dependency on its cotton into formal diplomatic recognition of the Confederate States of America.
p4.zh: 及时向1860年——美国内战前夕——向另一个具有历史意义的近乎垄断的供应商——美国棉花工业迈步前进. 当时,南方各州提供了英国进口棉花的大部分.南方希望脱离联盟,希望利用英国高度依赖其棉花的机会,正式外交承认美国联邦国。

p5.original: This leads us to this chapter's topic: a firm that controls all (or nearly all) of the supply of a good or service—a monopoly. How do monopoly firms behave in the marketplace? Do they have “power?” Does this power potentially have unintended consequences? We’ll return to this case at the end of the chapter to see how the tea and cotton monopolies influenced U.S. history.
p5.zh: 这使我们想到本章的主题:一个控制所有(或几乎所有)货物或服务供应的公司——一种垄断。垄断公司在市场上如何行为? 他们是否拥有“力量? ” 这种力量是否会产生意想不到的后果? 我们将会回到这个案子的结尾,

p7.original: In this chapter, you will learn about:

p8.original: How Monopolies form: Barriers to Entry
p8.zh: 垄断如何形成:进入壁垒

p9.original: How a Profit-Maximizing Monopoly Chooses Output and Price
p9.zh: 利润最大化的垄断如何选择产出和价格

p10.original: Many believe that top executives at firms are the strongest supporters of market competition, but this belief is far from the truth. Think about it this way: If you very much wanted to win an Olympic gold medal, would you rather be far better than everyone else, or locked in competition with many athletes just as good as you? Similarly, if you would like to attain a very high level of profits, would you rather manage a business with little or no competition, or struggle against many tough competitors who are trying to sell to your customers? By now, you might have read the chapter on Perfect Competition. In this chapter, we explore the opposite extreme: monopoly.
p10.zh: 许多人认为,公司高层高管是市场竞争的最强支持者,但这种信念远非事实.想想吧:如果你非常想赢得奥运会金牌,你会宁愿比其他人好得多,还是和你一样被锁在与许多运动员的竞争中? 同样,如果你想要获得很高的利润,你宁愿在很少或没有竞争的情况下管理一个企业,还是要与许多试图卖给你的客户的强硬竞争者斗争? 现在,你可能已经读过 关于完美竞争的一章。 在本章中,我们探索的是相反的极端:垄断。

p11.original: If perfect competition is a market where firms have no market power and they simply respond to the market price, monopoly is a market with no competition at all, and firms have a great deal of market power. In the case of monopoly, one firm produces all of the output in a market. Since a monopoly faces no significant competition, it can charge any price it wishes, subject to the demand curve. While a monopoly, by definition, refers to a single firm, in practice people often use the term to describe a market in which one firm merely has a very high market share. This tends to be the definition that the U.S. Department of Justice uses.
p11.zh: 如果完美的竞争是公司没有市场支配力的市场,而它们只是对市场价格作出反应,那么垄断是一个完全没有竞争的市场,公司拥有很大的市场支配力. 就垄断而言,一家公司在一个市场上生产所有产出。 由于垄断公司没有面临重大竞争,它可以收取任何它想要的价格,但需遵守需求曲线。 虽然从定义上讲,垄断是指单一的公司,但在实践中,人们常常使用这一术语来描述一个公司仅仅拥有很高市场份额的市场。 这往往是美国的定义.司法部使用.

p12.original: Even though there are very few true monopolies in existence, we do deal with some of those few every day, often without realizing it: The U.S. Postal Service, your electric, and garbage collection companies are a few examples. Some new drugs are produced by only one pharmaceutical firm—and no close substitutes for that drug may exist.
p12.zh: 尽管真正的垄断很少存在,但我们确实每天处理其中的少数,常常没有意识到这一点:美国。邮局,你的电机公司,垃圾收集公司都是几个例子. 有些新药只由一家制药公司生产,而且可能不存在这种药的近代药。

p13.original: From the mid-1990s until 2004, the U.S. Department of Justice prosecuted the Microsoft Corporation for including Internet Explorer as the default web browser with its operating system. The Justice Department’s argument was that, since Microsoft possessed an extremely high market share in the industry for operating systems, the inclusion of a free web browser constituted unfair competition to other browsers, such as Netscape Navigator. Since nearly everyone was using Windows, including Internet Explorer eliminated the incentive for consumers to explore other browsers and made it impossible for competitors to gain a foothold in the market. In 2013, the Windows system ran on more than 90% of the most commonly sold personal computers. In 2015, a U.S. federal court tossed out antitrust charges that Google had an agreement with mobile device makers to set Google as the default search engine.
p13.zh: 从1990年代中期一直到2004年,美国.司法部起诉微软公司将Internet Explorer列为其操作系统的默认网页浏览器.司法部的论点是,由于微软在操作系统行业中占有极高的市场份额,所以纳入免费网页浏览器构成与其他浏览器的不公平竞争,如Netscape导航. 由于几乎所有人都在使用Windows,包括Internet Explorer,取消了消费者探索其他浏览器的动机,使得竞争对手无法在市场上获得立足点.2013年,Windows系统运行在90%以上最常用的销售个人电脑上.2015年,一家美国联邦法院抛出反托拉斯指控,Google与移动设备制造商达成协议,将Google设定为默认搜索引擎.

p14.original: This chapter begins by describing how monopolies are protected from competition, including laws that prohibit competition, technological advantages, and certain configurations of demand and supply. It then discusses how a monopoly will choose its profit-maximizing quantity to produce and what price to charge. While a monopoly must be concerned about whether consumers will purchase its products or spend their money on something altogether different, the monopolist need not worry about the actions of other competing firms producing its products. As a result, a monopoly is not a price taker like a perfectly competitive firm, but instead exercises some power to choose its market price.
p14.zh: 本章首先描述了垄断如何受到保护免受竞争,包括禁止竞争的法律、技术优势以及某些供需的布局。 然后讨论垄断如何选择生产利润最大化的数量和收取什么价格。 虽然垄断必须关注消费者是购买其产品,还是把钱花在完全不同的东西上,但垄断者不必担心生产其产品的其他竞争公司的行动。 因此,垄断不是像一个完全有竞争力的公司那样的价格承受者,而是行使某种权力来选择其市场价格。

p15.original: How Monopolies Form: Barriers to Entry
p15.zh: 垄断形式如何:进入障碍

p16.original: Because of the lack of competition, monopolies tend to earn significant economic profits. These profits should attract vigorous competition as we described in Perfect Competition, and yet, because of one particular characteristic of monopoly, they do not. Barriers to entry are the legal, technological, or market forces that discourage or prevent potential competitors from entering a market. Barriers to entry can range from the simple and easily surmountable, such as the cost of renting retail space, to the extremely restrictive. For example, there are a finite number of radio frequencies available for broadcasting. Once an entrepreneur or firm has purchased the rights to all of them, no new competitors can enter the market.
p16.zh: 由于缺乏竞争,垄断往往能赚取可观的经济利润。 这些利润应该像我们在“完美竞争”中描述的那样吸引激烈的竞争,然而,由于垄断的某一特点,它们并没有吸引竞争。进入障碍是阻碍或阻止潜在竞争者进入市场的法律、技术或市场力量。进入障碍包括简单和容易克服的,例如租赁零售空间的费用,以及极其严格的限制。 例如,可供广播的无线电频率数量有限。 一旦一个企业家或公司购买了他们所有的权利,任何新的竞争者都无法进入市场。

p17.original: In some cases, barriers to entry may lead to monopoly. In other cases, they may limit competition to a few firms. Barriers may block entry even if the firm or firms currently in the market are earning profits. Thus, in markets with significant barriers to entry, it is not necessarily true that abnormally high profits will attract new firms, and that this entry of new firms will eventually cause the price to decline so that surviving firms earn only a normal level of profit in the long run.
p17.zh: 在某些情况下,进入壁垒可能导致垄断。 在其他情况下,它们可能将竞争限制在少数公司。 即使目前进入市场的公司在赚取利润,障碍也可能阻碍进入。 因此,在存在重大进入壁垒的市场中,非正常高利润不一定会吸引新的公司,而新公司的这种进入最终会导致价格下降,从而使幸存的公司从长远来看只能赚取正常水平的利润。

p18.original: There are five types of monopoly, based on the types of barriers to entry they exploit.
p18.zh: 根据其利用的进入壁垒类型,垄断有五种类型.

p20.original: Economies of scale can combine with the size of the market to limit competition. (We introduced this theme in Production, Cost and Industry Structure).  presents a long-run average cost curve for the airplane manufacturing industry. It shows economies of scale up to an output of 8,000 planes per year and a price of P0, then constant returns to scale from 8,000 to 20,000 planes per year, and diseconomies of scale at a quantity of production greater than 20,000 planes per year.
p20.zh: 规模经济可以与市场规模相结合,限制竞争.(我们在《生产、成本和工业结构》中介绍了这一主题)为飞机制造业提供了一个长期平均成本曲线。这表明规模经济每年产量达8000架飞机,价格为P0,然后不断回升,从每年8000架飞机到20000架飞机,规模经济不经济,产量超过20000架飞机.

p21.original: Now consider the market demand curve in the diagram, which intersects the long-run average cost (LRAC) curve at an output level of 5,000 planes per year and at a price P1, which is higher than P0. In this situation, the market has room for only one producer. If a second firm attempts to enter the market at a smaller size, say by producing a quantity of 4,000 planes, then its average costs will be higher than those of the existing firm, and it will be unable to compete. If the second firm attempts to enter the market at a larger size, like 8,000 planes per year, then it could produce at a lower average cost—but it could not sell all 8,000 planes that it produced because of insufficient demand in the market.
p21.zh: 现在考虑图中的市场需求曲线,它以每年5,000架飞机的产量水平和高于P0的P1价格,交叉了长期平均成本曲线(LRAC). 在这种情况下,市场只有1个生产者。 如果第二家公司试图以较小的规模进入市场,比如生产4000架飞机,那么其平均成本将高于现有公司的成本,因此无法竞争. 如果第二家公司试图以更大的规模进入市场,比如每年8 000架飞机,那么它可以以较低的平均成本生产,但是由于市场需求不足,它不能出售它生产的所有8 000架飞机。

p22.original: Economies of Scale and Natural Monopoly

p23.original: Economists call this situation, when economies of scale are large relative to the quantity demanded in the market, a natural monopoly. Natural monopolies often arise in industries where the marginal cost of adding an additional customer is very low, once the fixed costs of the overall system are in place. This results in situations where there are substantial economies of scale. For example, once a water company lays the main water pipes through a neighborhood, the marginal cost of providing water service to another home is fairly low. Once the electric company installs lines in a new subdivision, the marginal cost of providing additional electrical service to one more home is minimal. It would be costly and duplicative for a second water company to enter the market and invest in a whole second set of main water pipes, or for a second electricity company to enter the market and invest in a whole new set of electrical wires. These industries offer an example where, because of economies of scale, one producer can serve the entire market more efficiently than a number of smaller producers that would need to make duplicate physical capital investments.
p23.zh: 经济学家称这种情况是规模经济相对于市场要求的数量而言是巨大的,是一种自然垄断.自然垄断往往出现在行业中,一旦整个系统的固定成本到位,增加一个客户的边际成本就非常低。 这导致出现规模经济相当大的情况。 例如,一旦一家供水公司通过一个街区铺设主要供水管道,向另一家供水服务的边际成本就相当低。 一旦电力公司在一个新的分公司安装线路,向另一个家庭提供额外的电力服务的边际成本是最低的。 第二家水公司进入市场,投资第二套主要水管,或第二家电力公司进入市场,投资一套全新的电线,将成本高昂,重复性很大。 这些行业提供了一个实例,表明由于规模经济,一个生产者比一些需要重复进行实物资本投资的较小生产者能够更有效地服务整个市场。

p24.original: A natural monopoly can also arise in smaller local markets for products that are difficult to transport. For example, cement production exhibits economies of scale, and the quantity of cement demanded in a local area may not be much larger than what a single plant can produce. Moreover, the costs of transporting cement over land are high, and so a cement plant in an area without access to water transportation may be a natural monopoly.
p24.zh: 当地市场规模较小,难以运输的产品也可能出现自然垄断。 例如,水泥生产显示出规模经济,而当地所需水泥数量可能并不比单个工厂所能生产的数量大得多。 此外,在陆地上运输水泥的费用很高,因此,在无法使用水路运输的地区建造水泥厂可能是自然的垄断。

p26.original: Another type of monopoly occurs when a company has control of a scarce physical resource. In the U.S. economy, one historical example of this pattern occurred when ALCOA—the Aluminum Company of America—controlled most of the supply of bauxite, a key mineral used in making aluminum. Back in the 1930s, when ALCOA controlled most of the bauxite, other firms were simply unable to produce enough aluminum to compete.
p26.zh: 另一种垄断形式是当一家公司控制了稀缺的有形资源时。在美国经济中,这一模式的一个历史例子就是美国铝业公司ALCOA控制了铝矿的大部分供应,铝矿是铝制过程中使用的关键矿物。早在20世纪30年代,当ALCOA控制了大部分铝土时,其他公司根本无法生产足够的铝来竞争.

p27.original: As another example, the majority of global diamond production is controlled by DeBeers, a multi-national company that has mining and production operations in South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, and Canada. It also has exploration activities on four continents, while directing a worldwide distribution network of rough cut diamonds. Although in recent years they have experienced growing competition, their impact on the rough diamond market is still considerable.
p27.zh: 另一个例子是,全球大多数钻石生产由DeBeers公司控制,该公司是一家在南非、博茨瓦纳、纳米比亚和加拿大从事采矿和生产业务的多国公司。 它还在四大洲开展勘探活动,同时指导一个毛坯钻石全球分销网络。 尽管近年来它们的竞争日益激烈,但它们对毛坯钻石市场的影响仍然很大。

p29.original: For some products, the government erects barriers to entry by prohibiting or limiting competition. Under U.S. law, no organization but the U.S. Postal Service is legally allowed to deliver first-class mail. Many states or cities have laws or regulations that allow households a choice of only one electric company, one water company, and one company to pick up the garbage. Most legal monopolies are utilities—products necessary for everyday life—that are socially beneficial. As a consequence, the government allows producers to become regulated monopolies, to ensure that customers have access to an appropriate amount of these products or services. Additionally, legal monopolies are often subject to economies of scale, so it makes sense to allow only one provider.
p29.zh: 对于一些产品,政府通过禁止或限制竞争来设置进入壁垒. 根据美国法律,除了美国之外,没有组织.邮政局依法可以办理一等邮递业务. 许多州或城市都有法律或条例,允许家庭只选择一家电力公司、一家水公司和一家公司来取垃圾。 大多数法律垄断是公用事业,是日常生活所必需的产品,对社会有益。 因此,政府允许生产者成为受管制的垄断者,以确保客户能够获得适当数量的这些产品或服务。 此外,法律上的垄断往往受制于规模经济,因此只允许一个供应商是合理的。

p31.original: Innovation takes time and resources to achieve. Suppose a company invests in research and development and finds the cure for the common cold. In this world of near ubiquitous information, other companies could take the formula, produce the drug, and because they did not incur the costs of research and development (R&D), undercut the price of the company that discovered the drug. Given this possibility, many firms would choose not to invest in research and development, and as a result, the world would have less innovation. To prevent this from happening, the Constitution of the United States specifies in Article I, Section 8: “The Congress shall have Power . . . to Promote the Progress of Science and Useful Arts, by securing for limited Times to Authors and Inventors the Exclusive Right to their Writings and Discoveries.” Congress used this power to create the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, as well as the U.S. Copyright Office. A patent gives the inventor the exclusive legal right to make, use, or sell the invention for a limited time. In the United States, exclusive patent rights last for 20 years. The idea is to provide limited monopoly power so that innovative firms can recoup their investment in R&D, but then to allow other firms to produce the product more cheaply once the patent expires.
p31.zh: 创新需要时间和资源才能实现。假设一家公司投资研发,找到常见寒冷的解药. 在这个几乎无处不在的信息世界中,其他公司可以服用配方,生产药物,并且因为它们没有产生研发费用(R&D),降低了发现该药物的公司的价格. 鉴于这种可能性,许多公司将选择不投资于研究与发展,因此,世界的创新程度会降低。 为了防止这种情况发生,《美国宪法》第一条第8节规定:“国会将拥有权力......通过为作者和发明者争取有限的时间,确保作者和发明者享有其著作和发现的专属权利,促进科学和实用艺术的进步。”专利和商标局 以及美国版权局.专利赋予发明人有限时间制作,使用或出售发明的专属法律权利.在美国,独占专利权持续20年.其想法是提供有限的垄断权力,以便创新型公司能够收回对研发的投资,但一旦专利到期,其他公司可以更便宜地生产产品。

p32.original: A trademark is an identifying symbol or name for a particular good, like Chiquita bananas, Chevrolet cars, or the Nike “swoosh” that appears on shoes and athletic gear. Between 2003 and 2019, roughly 6.8 million trademarks were registered with the U.S. government. A firm can renew a trademark repeatedly, as long as it remains in active use.
p32.zh: 商标是某种特定商品的识别符号或名称,例如Chiquita香蕉、Chevrolet汽车或鞋和运动用具上出现的耐克“swoush”。2003年至2019年间,大约有680万个商标在美国政府注册.企业可以多次续展商标,只要该商标仍在积极使用.

p33.original: A copyright, according to the U.S. Copyright Office, “is a form of protection provided by the laws of the United States for ‘original works of authorship’ including literary, dramatic, musical, architectural, cartographic, choreographic, pantomimic, pictorial, graphic, sculptural, and audiovisual creations.” No one can reproduce, display, or perform a copyrighted work without the author's permission. Copyright protection ordinarily lasts for the life of the author plus 70 years.
p33.zh: 美国认为是版权.版权局,“是美国法律为`原作者作品 ' 提供的一种保护形式,包括文学、戏剧、音乐、建筑、制图、舞蹈、胰腺、图片、图形、雕塑和视听创作。 ”未经作者许可,任何人不得复制、展示或表演版权作品。版权保护通常持续到作者的寿命加上70年。

p34.original: Roughly speaking, patent law covers inventions and copyright protects books, songs, and art. However, in certain areas, like the invention of new software, it has been unclear whether patent or copyright protection should apply. There is also a body of law known as trade secrets. Even if a company does not have a patent on an invention, competing firms are not allowed to steal their secrets. One famous trade secret is the formula for Coca-Cola, which is not protected under copyright or patent law, but is simply kept secret by the company.
p34.zh: 简言之,专利法涵盖发明,版权保护书籍、歌曲和艺术。 然而,在某些领域,如新软件的发明,专利或版权保护是否应当适用一直不清楚. 还有一套法律被称为商业秘密。 即使公司对某项发明没有专利权,竞合公司也不得窃取其秘密. 一个著名的贸易秘密是可口可乐的配方,它不受版权或专利法的保护,而只是被公司保密.

p35.original: Taken together, we call this combination of patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secret law intellectual property, because it implies ownership over an idea, concept, or image, not a physical piece of property like a house or a car. Countries around the world have enacted laws to protect intellectual property, although the time periods and exact provisions of such laws vary across countries. There are ongoing negotiations, both through the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) and through international treaties, to bring greater harmony to the intellectual property laws of different countries to determine the extent to which those in other countries will respect patents and copyrights of those in other countries.
p35.zh: 我们把专利、商标、版权和贸易秘密法知识产权称为这种结合,因为它意味着对一个想法、概念或形象的所有权,而不是像房屋或汽车一样的有形财产。世界各国都颁布了保护知识产权的法律,尽管各国这些法律的时间和确切规定各不相同。目前正通过世界知识产权组织(知识产权组织)和国际条约进行谈判,以进一步协调不同国家的知识产权法,确定其他国家的知识产权法在多大程度上尊重其他国家的知识产权和版权。

p36.original: Government limitations on competition used to be more common in the United States. For most of the twentieth century, only one phone company—AT&T—was legally allowed to provide local and long distance service. From the 1930s to the 1970s, one set of federal regulations limited which destinations airlines could choose to fly to and what fares they could charge. Another set of regulations limited the interest rates that banks could pay to depositors; yet another specified how much trucking firms could charge customers.
p36.zh: 政府对竞争的限制在美国过去更为普遍。 在20世纪的大部分时间里,只有一家电话公司——AT&T——在法律上被允许提供当地和长途服务。 从20世纪30年代到70年代,一套联邦条例限制哪些目的地的航空公司可以选择飞往哪些目的地以及它们可以收取多少票价。另一套条例限制银行可以向存款人支付的利率;还有一套条例具体规定了卡车公司可以向客户收取多少费用。

p37.original:
What products we consider utilities depends, in part, on the available technology. Fifty years ago,
 telephone companies provided local and long distance service over wires. It did not make much sense to have many companies building multiple wiring systems across towns and the entire country. AT&T lost its monopoly on long distance service when the technology for providing phone service changed from wires to microwave and satellite transmission, so that multiple firms could use the same transmission mechanism. The same thing happened to local service, especially in recent years, with the growth in cellular phone systems.
p37.zh: 我们认为什么产品是公用事业部分取决于现有技术。50年前,电话公司通过电线提供当地和长途服务。 许多公司在城镇和全国建立多条线路系统是没有道理的。AT&T失去了对长途服务的垄断,因为提供电话服务的技术从电线变为微波和卫星传输,这样多家公司就可以使用同样的传输机制.当地服务也发生了同样的情况,特别是近年来移动电话系统的增长。

p38.original: The combination of improvements in production technologies and a general sense that the markets could provide services adequately led to a wave of deregulation, starting in the late 1970s and continuing into the 1990s. This wave eliminated or reduced government restrictions on the firms that could enter, the prices that they could charge, and the quantities that many industries could produce, including telecommunications, airlines, trucking, banking, and electricity.
p38.zh: 生产技术的改进与市场能够充分提供服务这一普遍认识相结合,导致了从1970年代末开始并持续到1990年代的放松管制浪潮。 这一浪潮消除或减少了政府对可以进入的公司、它们可以收取的价格以及许多行业,包括电信、航空公司、卡车运输、银行业和电力业可以生产的数量的限制。

p39.original: Around the world, from Europe to Latin America to Africa and Asia, many governments continue to control and limit competition in what those governments perceive to be key industries, including airlines, banks, steel companies, oil companies, and telephone companies.
p39.zh: 在世界各地,从欧洲到拉丁美洲到非洲和亚洲,许多国家的政府继续控制和限制这些政府认为是关键行业的竞争,包括航空公司、银行、钢铁公司、石油公司和电话公司。

p40.original: Vist this website for examples of some pretty bizarre patents.
p40.zh: 看看这个网站, 以举例说明一些相当奇怪的专利。

p42.original: Businesses have developed a number of schemes for creating barriers to entry by deterring potential competitors from entering the market. One method is known as predatory pricing, in which a firm uses the threat of sharp price cuts to discourage competition. Predatory pricing is a violation of U.S. antitrust law, but it is difficult to prove.
p42.zh: 企业制定了一些计划,通过阻止潜在竞争者进入市场来制造进入壁垒。一种方法被称为掠夺性定价,其中一家公司利用大幅削减价格的威胁来阻止竞争.掠夺性定价违反美国反托拉斯法,但难以证明.

p43.original: Consider a large airline that provides most of the flights between two particular cities. A new, small start-up airline decides to offer service between these two cities. The large airline immediately slashes prices on this route to the bone, so that the new entrant cannot make any money. After the new entrant has gone out of business, the incumbent firm can raise prices again.
p43.zh: 考虑一个大型航空公司,提供两个特定城市之间的大部分航班.一个新的,小型的起动航空公司决定提供这两座城市之间的服务.大型航空公司在这条航线上立即将价格跌至骨骼,以致新进的机身无法赚到任何钱. 新进公司停业后,现职公司可以再次提价.

p44.original: After the company repeats this pattern once or twice, potential new entrants may decide that it is not wise to try to compete. Small airlines often accuse larger airlines of predatory pricing: in the early 2000s, for example, ValuJet accused Delta of predatory pricing, Frontier accused United, and Reno Air accused Northwest. In 2015, the Justice Department ruled against American Express and Mastercard for imposing restrictions on retailers that encouraged customers to use lower swipe fees on credit transactions.
p44.zh: 在公司重复过一次或两次这种模式之后,潜在的新进入者可能会决定尝试竞争是不明智的. 小航空公司经常指责较大的航空公司进行掠夺性定价:例如,2000年代初,ValuJet指控德尔塔进行掠夺性定价,Frontier指控United,Reno Air指控西北.2015年,司法部裁定美国快报和Mastercard公司对鼓励客户在信用交易中使用较低刷卡费的零售商施加限制.

p45.original: In some cases, large advertising budgets can also act as a way of discouraging the competition. If the only way to launch a successful new national cola drink is to spend more than the promotional budgets of Coca-Cola and Pepsi Cola, not too many companies will try. A firmly established brand name can be difficult to dislodge.
p45.zh: 在某些情况下,大型广告预算也可起到抑制竞争的作用。 如果成功推出新国产可乐饮料的唯一办法,是花费比可口可乐和百事可乐的促销预算还要多,那么不会有太多的公司会尝试.牢固确定的品牌名称可能难以拆散.

p47.original: lists the barriers to entry that we have discussed. This list is not exhaustive, since firms have proved to be highly creative in inventing business practices that discourage competition. When barriers to entry exist, perfect competition is no longer a reasonable description of how an industry works. When barriers to entry are high enough, monopoly can result.
p47.zh: 列出我们讨论过的进入障碍。这份清单并非详尽无遗,因为事实证明,公司在发明抑制竞争的商业做法方面很有创意。 当存在进入壁垒时,完美的竞争就不再是对一个行业如何运作的合理描述. 当进入壁垒足够高时,就会产生垄断。

p53.zh: 政府往往以监管(或所有权)回应

p68.original: Barriers to entry prevent or discourage competitors from entering the market. These barriers include: economies of scale that lead to natural monopoly; control of a physical resource; legal restrictions on competition; patent, trademark and copyright protection; and practices to intimidate the competition like predatory pricing. Intellectual property refers to legally guaranteed ownership of an idea, rather than a physical item. The laws that protect intellectual property include patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets. A natural monopoly arises when economies of scale persist over a large enough range of output that if one firm supplies the entire market, no other firm can enter without facing a cost disadvantage.
p68.zh: 进入壁垒阻碍或阻止竞争者进入市场。 这些障碍包括:导致自然垄断的规模经济;对物质资源的控制;对竞争的法律限制;专利、商标和版权保护;以及恐吓竞争的做法,如掠夺性定价。知识产权是指对某一想法的法律保障所有权,而不是实物。保护知识产权的法律包括专利、版权、商标以及商业秘密。 当规模经济持续维持在足够大的范围的产出上时,自然就会出现垄断,如果一家公司供应整个市场,任何其他公司都无法进入,而不会面临成本劣势。

p74.original: Suppose the local electrical utility, a legal monopoly based on economies of scale, was split into four firms of equal size, with the idea that eliminating the monopoly would promote competitive pricing of electricity. What do you anticipate would happen to prices?
p74.zh: 假设以规模经济为基础的法律垄断的当地电力公用事业被分成大小相同的四家公司,其想法是消除垄断将促进电价的竞争性。 你预计价格会怎样?

p75.zh: 由于规模经济,每个公司的平均成本将高于以往。(他们各自必须建造自己的电线. )结果,他们各自必须提高价格以支付较高的成本.政策会失败的。

p94.original: How a Profit-Maximizing Monopoly Chooses Output and Price
p94.zh: 利润最大化的垄断如何选择产出和价格

p95.original: Consider a monopoly firm, comfortably surrounded by barriers to entry so that it need not fear competition from other producers. How will this monopoly choose its profit-maximizing quantity of output, and what price will it charge? Profits for the monopolist, like any firm, will be equal to total revenues minus total costs. We can analyze the pattern of costs for the monopoly within the same framework as the costs of a perfectly competitive firm—that is, by using total cost, fixed cost, variable cost, marginal cost, average cost, and average variable cost. However, because a monopoly faces no competition, its situation and its decision process will differ from that of a perfectly competitive firm. (The Clear It Up feature discusses how hard it is sometimes to define “market” in a monopoly situation.)
p95.zh: 考虑一个垄断公司,在进入方面受到障碍的舒适包围,这样它就不必害怕其他生产商的竞争。 这种垄断将如何选择其利润最大化的产出数量,并将收取什么价格?垄断者的利润与任何公司一样,将等于总收入减去总成本。 我们可以在与完全具有竞争力的公司的成本相同的框架内分析垄断的成本模式,即利用总成本、固定成本、可变成本、边际成本、平均成本和平均可变成本。 然而,由于垄断没有面临竞争,其状况和决策过程将不同于完全具有竞争力的公司。(Clear Up的特征讨论了在垄断情况下界定“市场”有时有多难。 )

p96.zh: 完全有竞争力的公司和垄断集团所看到的需求曲线

p97.original: A perfectly competitive firm acts as a price taker, so we calculate total revenue taking the given market price and multiplying it by the quantity of output that the firm chooses. The demand curve as it is perceived by a perfectly competitive firm appears in  (a). The flat perceived demand curve means that, from the viewpoint of the perfectly competitive firm, it could sell either a relatively low quantity like Ql or a relatively high quantity like Qh at the market price P.

p98.zh: 完美竞争者与垄断者的感知需求曲线

p100.original: A monopoly is a firm that sells all or nearly all of the goods and services in a given market. However, what defines the “market”?
p100.zh: 垄断是指在一个特定市场中销售全部或几乎所有货物和服务的公司。 然而,“市场”的定义是什么?

p101.original: In a famous 1947 case, the federal government accused the DuPont company of having a monopoly in the cellophane market, pointing out that DuPont produced 75% of the cellophane in the United States. DuPont countered that even though it had a 75% market share in cellophane, it had less than a 20% share of the “flexible packaging materials,” which includes all other moisture-proof papers, films, and foils. In 1956, after years of legal appeals, the U.S. Supreme Court held that the broader market definition was more appropriate, and it dismissed the case against DuPont.
p101.zh: 在1947年的著名案件中,联邦政府指责杜邦公司垄断大提琴市场,指出杜邦公司在美国生产75%的大提琴.DuPont反驳说,尽管它在大提琴中拥有75%的市场份额,但它在“软包装材料”中的份额不到20%,其中包括所有其他防湿的纸张、胶片和胶片。1956年,经过多年的法律上诉,美国.最高法院认为,更广泛的市场定义更合适,因此驳回了DuPont一案.

p102.original: Questions over how to define the market continue today. True, Microsoft in the 1990s had a dominant share of the software for computer operating systems, but in the total market for all computer software and services, including everything from games to scientific programs, the Microsoft share was only about 14% in 2014. The Greyhound bus company may have a near-monopoly on the market for intercity bus transportation, but it is only a small share of the market for intercity transportation if that market includes private cars, airplanes, and railroad service. DeBeers has a monopoly in diamonds, but it is a much smaller share of the total market for precious gemstones and an even smaller share of the total market for jewelry. A small town in the country may have only one gas station: is this gas station a “monopoly,” or does it compete with gas stations that might be five, 10, or 50 miles away?
p102.zh: 如何定义市场的问题今天还在继续。诚然,微软在20世纪90年代在计算机操作系统的软件中占有主导份额,但在所有计算机软件和服务的总市场中,包括从游戏到科学程序的一切,微软份额在2014年只有14%左右.灰狗巴士公司在城际巴士运输市场上可能存在近乎垄断的情况,但如果该市场包括私人汽车,飞机,铁路服务,它只是城际运输市场的一小部分.德比尔斯公司对钻石拥有垄断权,但在珍贵宝石的总市场中,它所占的份额要小得多,在珠宝总市场中所占的份额还要小得多.这个国家的小镇可能只有一个加油站:这个加油站是“垄断的”,还是与五、十或五十英里外的加油站竞争?

p103.original: In general, if a firm produces a product without close substitutes, then we can consider the firm a monopoly producer in a single market. However, if buyers have a range of similar—even if not identical—options available from other firms, then the firm is not a monopoly. Still, arguments over whether substitutes are close or not close can be controversial.
p103.zh: 一般而言,如果一家公司生产的产品没有近乎的替代品,那么我们可以将该公司视为单一市场的垄断生产者. 但是,如果买方有其他公司提供的一系列类似——即使不是完全相同的——选择,那么公司就不是垄断。 然而,关于替代物是否接近的论点仍可引起争议。

p104.original: While a monopolist can charge any price for its product, nonetheless the demand for the firm’s product constrains the price. No monopolist, even one that is thoroughly protected by high barriers to entry, can require consumers to purchase its product. Because the monopolist is the only firm in the market, its demand curve is the same as the market demand curve, which is, unlike that for a perfectly competitive firm, downward-sloping.
p104.zh: 虽然垄断者可以对其产品收取任何价格,但对公司产品的需求却限制了价格。任何垄断者,即使是受到高进入壁垒的彻底保护的垄断者,都不能要求消费者购买其产品。 由于垄断公司是市场上唯一的公司,其需求曲线与市场需求曲线相同,这与完全具有竞争力的公司不同,后者向下倾斜。

p105.original: illustrates this situation. The monopolist can either choose a point like R with a low price (Pl) and high quantity (Qh), or a point like S with a high price (Ph) and a low quantity (Ql), or some intermediate point. Setting the price too high will result in a low quantity sold, and will not bring in much revenue. Conversely, setting the price too low may result in a high quantity sold, but because of the low price, it will not bring in much revenue either. The challenge for the monopolist is to strike a profit-maximizing balance between the price it charges and the quantity that it sells. However, why isn’t the perfectly competitive firm’s demand curve also the market demand curve? See the following Clear It Up feature for the answer to this question.
p105.zh: 说明这种情况。独占者可以选择像R一样的低价(Pl)和高量(Qh)的点,也可以选择像S那样的高价(Ph)和低量(Ql)的点,或者选择某种中间点.定价过高将导致销售量低,不会带来多少收入。反之,规定价格过低可能导致销售量高,但由于价格低,也不会带来多少收入。垄断者面临的挑战是在它收取的价格与它销售的数量之间实现利润最大化的平衡。 但为何完全具有竞争力的公司的需求曲线不是市场需求曲线?这个问题的答案见以下Clear It Up特征。

p106.original: What is the difference between perceived demand and market demand?
p106.zh: 所预见的需求与市场需求有何区别?

p107.original: The demand curve as perceived by a perfectly competitive firm is not the overall market demand curve for that product. However, the firm’s demand curve as perceived by a monopoly is the same as the market demand curve. The reason for the difference is that each perfectly competitive firm perceives the demand for its products in a market that includes many other firms. In effect, the demand curve perceived by a perfectly competitive firm is a tiny slice of the entire market demand curve. In contrast, a monopoly perceives demand for its product in a market where the monopoly is the only producer.
p107.zh: 一个完全有竞争力的公司所认为的需求曲线不是该产品的总体市场需求曲线。 然而,垄断所认为的公司需求曲线与市场需求曲线相同。造成这种差异的原因是,每一个完全具有竞争力的公司都认识到在包括许多其他公司在内的市场上对其产品的需求。 实际上,完全具有竞争力的公司所看到的需求曲线是整个市场需求曲线的一小部分。与此相反,垄断在垄断是唯一生产者的市场中,对它的产品的需求。

p108.original: Total Cost and Total Revenue for a Monopolist
p108.zh: 垄断者的费用总额和总收入

The total cost curve has its typical shape that we learned about in Production, Costs and Industry Structure, and that we used in Perfect Competition; that is, total costs rise and the curve grows steeper as output increases, as the final column of  shows.

p110.zh: 保健券垄断收入总额和总费用

p111.zh: 保健费用总额和总收入

p148.original: Total revenue, though, is different.  Since a monopolist faces a downward sloping demand curve, the only way it can sell more output is by reducing its price.  Selling more output raises revenue, but lowering price reduces it.  Thus, the shape of total revenue isn’t clear.  Let’s explore this using the data in  , which shows quantities along the demand curve and the price at each quantity demanded, and then calculates total revenue by multiplying price times quantity at each level of output. (In this example, we give the output as 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on, for the sake of simplicity. If you prefer a dash of greater realism, you can imagine that the pharmaceutical company measures these output levels and the corresponding prices per 1,000 or 10,000 pills.) As the figure illustrates, total revenue for a monopolist has the shape of a hill, first rising, next flattening out, and then falling. In this example, total revenue is highest at a quantity of 6 or 7.
p148.zh: 不过,总收入是不同的。 由于垄断者面临向下倾斜的需求曲线,它能够销售更多产出的唯一办法是降低其价格。出售更多的产出可以增加收入,但降低价格则会降低收入。 因此,总收入的形态并不明确。 让我们用其中的数据来探讨这个问题,这些数据显示需求曲线上的数量和要求的每个数量的价格,然后通过将每个产出水平的价格乘以数量计算总收入。(在此例子中,我们给出产出为1,2,3,4等,以简单为目的). 如果你更喜欢更现实的一瞬间,你可以想象制药公司会测量这些产出水平和相应的每1000或10,000个药丸的价格。 )如图所示,独占者的收入总额有山形,首先上升,接下来平缓,然后下降。 在这个例子中,总收入最高,为6或7。

p149.original: However, the monopolist is not seeking to maximize revenue, but instead to earn the highest possible profit. In the HealthPill example in , the highest profit will occur at the quantity where total revenue is the farthest above total cost. This looks to be somewhere in the middle of the graph, but where exactly?  It is easier to see the profit maximizing level of output by using the marginal approach, to which we turn next.
p149.zh: 然而,垄断者并不寻求实现收入最大化,而是争取获得尽可能高的利润. 在健康中心的例子中,最高利润将发生在总收入比总成本最高的金额上。 这似乎是在图表中间的某个地方, 但具体在哪里?利用边际方法(我们转向边际方法),更容易看到利润最大化的产出水平。

p150.original: Marginal Revenue and Marginal Cost for a Monopolist
p150.zh: 垄断者边际收入和边际成本

p151.original: In the real world, a monopolist often does not have enough information to analyze its entire total revenues or total costs curves. After all, the firm does not know exactly what would happen if it were to alter production dramatically. However, a monopolist often has fairly reliable information about how changing output by small or moderate amounts will affect its marginal revenues and marginal costs, because it has had experience with such changes over time and because modest changes are easier to extrapolate from current experience. A monopolist can use information on marginal revenue and marginal cost to seek out the profit-maximizing combination of quantity and price.
p151.zh: 在现实世界中,一个垄断者往往没有足够的信息来分析其全部总收入或总成本曲线.毕竟,如果公司大幅度改变生产,公司并不知道会发生什么。 然而,一个垄断者往往有相当可靠的信息,说明小量或中量产出的变化将如何影响其边际收入和边际成本,因为它在一段时间内就有过这种变化的经验,而且从目前的经验中可以比较容易地推断出一些小的变化。垄断者可以利用关于边际收入和边际成本的信息来寻找数量和价格的利润最大化组合.

p152.original: expands  using the figures on total costs and total revenues from the HealthPill example to calculate marginal revenue and marginal cost. This monopoly faces typical upward-sloping marginal cost and downward-sloping marginal revenue curves, as  shows.
p152.zh: 利用卫生福利方案实例中的总成本和总收入数字来计算边际收入和边际成本。 如所示,这种垄断面临典型的向上倾斜的边际成本和向下倾斜的边际收入曲线。

p153.original: Notice that marginal revenue is zero at a quantity of 7, and turns negative at quantities higher than 7. It may seem counterintuitive that marginal revenue could ever be zero or negative: after all, doesn't an increase in quantity sold not always mean more revenue? For a perfect competitor, each additional unit sold brought a positive marginal revenue, because marginal revenue was equal to the given market price. However, a monopolist can sell a larger quantity and see a decline in total revenue. When a monopolist increases sales by one unit, it gains some marginal revenue from selling that extra unit, but also loses some marginal revenue because it must now sell every other unit at a lower price. As the quantity sold becomes higher, at some point the drop in price is proportionally more than the increase in greater quantity of sales, causing a situation where more sales bring in less revenue. In other words, marginal revenue is negative.
p153.zh: 注意边际收入为零,数量为7,数量高于7,变为负数.边际收入可能永远是零或负的,这看起来可能适得其反:毕竟,销售量的增加并非总意味着更多的收入吗? 对于一个完美的竞争者来说,每个额外的出售单位都带来了正边际收入,因为边际收入等于给定的市场价格. 然而,垄断者可以出售数量较多的商品,并看到总收入的下降. 当一个垄断者增加一个单位的销售时,它从出售该额外单位中获得一些边际收入,但也因为现在它必须以较低的价格出售每一个其他单位而损失一些边际收入. 随着销售量的上升,价格的下降在某个时候比销售量的增加要大,造成销售量的增加带来收入减少的局面。换言之,边际收入是负的。

p154.original: Marginal Revenue and Marginal Cost for the HealthPill Monopoly
p154.zh: 保健中心垄断的边际收入和边际费用

p201.original: A monopolist can determine its profit-maximizing price and quantity by analyzing the marginal revenue and marginal costs of producing an extra unit. If the marginal revenue exceeds the marginal cost, then the firm should produce the extra unit.
p201.zh: 垄断者可以通过分析生产额外单位的边际收入和边际成本,确定其利润最大化的价格和数量。 如果边际收入超过边际成本,那么公司应当生产额外单位.

p202.original: For example, at an output of 4 in , marginal revenue is 600 and marginal cost is 250, so producing this unit will clearly add to overall profits. At an output of 5, marginal revenue is 400 and marginal cost is 400, so producing this unit still means overall profits are unchanged. However, expanding output from 5 to 6 would involve a marginal revenue of 200 and a marginal cost of 850, so that sixth unit would actually reduce profits. Thus, the monopoly can tell from the marginal revenue and marginal cost that of the choices in the table, the profit-maximizing level of output is 5.
p202.zh: 例如,在产出为4 in 时,边际收入为600,边际成本为250,因此生产这个单位显然会增加总体利润. 在产出5时,边际收入为400,边际成本为400,因此生产这个单位仍然意味着总体利润没有变化. 然而,将产出从5增加到6将涉及200的边际收入和850的边际成本,因此第六单位实际上会减少利润. 因此,从表中选择的边际收入和边际成本可以看出垄断,利润最大化的产出水平为5。

p203.original: The monopoly could seek out the profit-maximizing level of output by increasing quantity by a small amount, calculating marginal revenue and marginal cost, and then either increasing output as long as marginal revenue exceeds marginal cost or reducing output if marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue. This process works without any need to calculate total revenue and total cost. Thus, a profit-maximizing monopoly should follow the rule of producing up to the quantity where marginal revenue is equal to marginal cost—that is, MR = MC. This quantity is easy to identify graphically, where MR and MC intersect.
p203.zh: 垄断可以通过少量增加数量,计算边际收入和边际成本,从而寻找产出的利润最大化水平,然后,只要边际收入超过边际成本,就可以增加产出,或者如果边际成本超过边际收入,就可以减少产出。 这个过程的运行不需要计算总收入和总成本. 因此,利润最大化的垄断应该遵循生产量达到边际收入等于边际成本(即MR = MC)的规则。 这种数量很容易以图形方式识别MR和MC交汇之处.

p205.original: If you find it counterintuitive that producing where marginal revenue equals marginal cost will maximize profits, working through the numbers will help.
p205.zh: 如果你发现产生边际收入等于边际成本 就能实现利润最大化, 通过数字工作会有所帮助。

p210.original: Marginal Revenue, Marginal Cost, Marginal and Total Profit
p210.zh: 边际收入、边际成本、边际和总利润

p256.original: repeats the marginal cost and marginal revenue data from , and adds two more columns: Marginal profit is the profitability of each additional unit sold. We define it as marginal revenue minus marginal cost. Finally, total profit is the sum of marginal profits. As long as marginal profit is positive, producing more output will increase total profits. When marginal profit turns negative, producing more output will decrease total profits. Total profit is maximized where marginal revenue equals marginal cost. In this example, maximum profit occurs at 5 units of output.
p256.zh: 重复来自.的边际成本和边际收入数据,并增加两栏:边际利润是每个额外售出的单位的利润率。 我们将其定义为边际收入减去边际成本。 最后,总利润是边际利润的总和. 只要边际利润为正值,生产更多的产出将增加利润总额. 当边际利润变为负值时,生产更多的产出会减少总利润. 如果边际收入等于边际成本,则利润总额最大化。 在这个例子中,最大利润发生在5个产出单位.

p257.original: A perfectly competitive firm will also find its profit-maximizing level of output where MR = MC. The key difference with a perfectly competitive firm is that in the case of perfect competition, marginal revenue is equal to price (MR = P), while for a monopolist, marginal revenue is not equal to the price, because changes in quantity of output affect the price.
p257.zh: 完全具有竞争力的公司也会发现其利润最大化的产出水平在MR = MC。与完全竞争的公司的主要区别在于,在完全竞争的情况下,边际收入等于价格(MR = P),而对于垄断者来说,边际收入则不等于价格,因为产出数量的变化影响价格.

p305.original: Illustrating Profits at the HealthPill Monopoly
p305.zh: 在保健中心独资店展示利润

p306.original: illustrates the three-step process where a monopolist: selects the profit-maximizing quantity to produce; decides what price to charge; determines total revenue, total cost, and profit.
p306.zh: 说明一个垄断者的三步进程:选择利润最大化的数量生产;决定收取的价格;确定总收入、总成本和利润。

p307.original: Step 1: The Monopolist Determines Its Profit-Maximizing Level of Output
p307.zh: 步骤1:垄断者确定其利润-最大产出水平

p308.original: The firm can use the points on the demand curve D to calculate total revenue, and then, based on total revenue, calculate its marginal revenue curve. The profit-maximizing quantity will occur where MR = MC—or at the last possible point before marginal costs start exceeding marginal revenue. On , MR = MC occurs at an output of 5.

p309.original: Step 2: The Monopolist Decides What Price to Charge
p309.zh: 第2步:垄断者决定收取什么价格

p310.original: The monopolist will charge what the market is willing to pay. A dotted line drawn straight up from the profit-maximizing quantity to the demand curve shows the profit-maximizing price which, in , is $800. This price is above the average cost curve, which shows that the firm is earning profits.
p310.zh: 垄断者将收取市场愿意支付的费用。 从利润最大化的数量直线到需求曲线的点线显示利润最大化的价格,以800美元计。 这一价格高于平均成本曲线,这表明公司正在赚取利润。

p311.original: Step 3: Calculate Total Revenue, Total Cost, and Profit
p311.zh: 第3步:计算收入总额、成本总额和利润

p312.original:
Total revenue is the overall shaded box, where the width of the box is the quantity sold and the height is the price. In , this is 5 x $800 = $4000. In , the bottom part of the shaded box, which is shaded more lightly, shows total costs; that is, quantity on the horizontal axis multiplied by average cost on the vertical axis or 5 x $330 = $1650. The larger box of total revenues minus the smaller box of total costs will equal profits, which the darkly shaded box shows. Using the numbers gives $4000 - $1650 = $2350.
In a perfectly competitive market, the forces of entry would erode this profit in the long run. However, a monopolist is protected by barriers to entry. In fact, one obvious sign of a possible monopoly is when a firm earns profits year after year, while doing more or less the same thing, without ever seeing increased competition eroding those profits.

p313.original: How a Profit-Maximizing Monopoly Decides Price

p314.original: Why is a monopolist’s marginal revenue always less than the price?
p314.zh: 为什么垄断者的边际收入总是低于价格?

p315.original: The marginal revenue curve for a monopolist always lies beneath the market demand curve. To understand why, think about increasing the quantity along the demand curve by one unit, so that you take one step down the demand curve to a slightly higher quantity but a slightly lower price. A demand curve is not sequential: It is not that first we sell Q1 at a higher price, and then we sell Q2 at a lower price. Rather, a demand curve is conditional: If we charge the higher price, we would sell Q1. If, instead, we charge a lower price (on all the units that we sell), we would sell Q2.
p315.zh: 垄断者的边际收入曲线始终位于市场需求曲线之下。 要了解原因,考虑将需求曲线上的数量增加一个单位,这样你就可以把需求曲线下移一步,到数量稍高但价格稍低. 一个需求曲线不是顺序的:不是首先我们以更高的价格出售Q1,然后我们以较低的价格出售Q2. 相反,一个需求曲线是有条件的:如果我们收取更高的价格,我们就会出售Q1. 如果反之,我们收取较低的价格(对于我们出售的所有单位),我们将出售问题2。

p316.original: When we think about increasing the quantity sold by one unit, marginal revenue is affected in two ways. First, we sell one additional unit at the new market price. Second, all the previous units, which we sold at the higher price, now sell for less. Because of the lower price on all units sold, the marginal revenue of selling a unit is less than the price of that unit—and the marginal revenue curve is below the demand curve. Tip: For a straight-line demand curve, MR and demand have the same vertical intercept.  As output increases, marginal revenue decreases twice as fast as demand, so that the horizontal intercept of MR is halfway to the horizontal intercept of demand. You can see this in the .
p316.zh: 当我们考虑增加一个单位销售的数量时,边际收入受到两种方式的影响. 一,按新市价再售一股. 二,我们以较高价格出售的以前所有单位,现在都卖得更少. 由于售出的所有单位的价格较低,售出一个单位的边际收入低于该单位的价格——边际收入曲线低于需求曲线.提示:对于直线需求曲线,MR和需求有相同的垂直截击. 随着产出的增加,边际收入的下降速度比需求快一倍,因此MR的横向截击距离横向截击需求还有一半. 你可以看到这一点在。

p317.original: The Monopolist’s Marginal Revenue Curve versus Demand Curve
p317.zh: 垄断者的边际收入曲线与需求曲线

p319.original: Most people criticize monopolies because they charge too high a price, but what economists object to is that monopolies do not supply enough output to be allocatively efficient. To understand why a monopoly is inefficient, it is useful to compare it with the benchmark model of perfect competition.
p319.zh: 大多数人批评垄断,因为他们收取过高的价格,但经济学家反对的是垄断不能提供足够的产出来分配效率。 为了理解垄断为何效率低下,有必要将其与完美竞争的基准模式进行比较。

p320.original: Allocative efficiency is an economic concept regarding efficiency at the social or societal level. It refers to producing the optimal quantity of some output, the quantity where the marginal benefit to society of one more unit just equals the marginal cost. The rule of profit maximization in a world of perfect competition was for each firm to produce the quantity of output where P = MC, where the price (P) is a measure of how much buyers value the good and the marginal cost (MC) is a measure of what marginal units cost society to produce. Following this rule assures allocative efficiency. If P > MC, then the marginal benefit to society (as measured by P) is greater than the marginal cost to society of producing additional units, and a greater quantity should be produced. However, in the case of monopoly, price is always greater than marginal cost at the profit-maximizing level of output, as you can see by looking back at . Thus, consumers do not benefit from a monopoly because it will sell a lower quantity in the market, at a higher price, than would have been the case in a perfectly competitive market.
p320.zh: 分配效率是一个关于社会或社会一级效率的经济概念。 它指的是生产一些产出的最佳数量,即一个多单元给社会的边际利益仅仅等于边际成本的数量。 在竞争完美的世界中,利润最大化的规则是每个公司生产产出的数量,其中P=MC,价格(P)是衡量买方价值多少的商品和边际成本(MC)是衡量社会生产成本的边际单位。 按照这项规则,确保分配效率。 如果P > MC,那么对社会的边际利益(按P衡量)大于生产额外单位对社会的边际成本,并且应该生产更多的量. 然而,在垄断的情况下,价格总是大于边际成本,在利润最大化的产出水平上,你可以回顾一下......。 因此,消费者不会从垄断中获益,因为垄断将比在竞争激烈的市场上销售数量低,价格更高。

p321.original: The problem of inefficiency for monopolies often runs even deeper than these issues, and also involves incentives for efficiency over longer periods of time. There are counterbalancing incentives here. On one side, firms may strive for new inventions and new intellectual property because they want to become monopolies and earn high profits—at least for a few years until the competition catches up. In this way, monopolies may come to exist because of competitive pressures on firms. However, once a barrier to entry is in place, a monopoly that does not need to fear competition can just produce the same old products in the same old way—while still ringing up a healthy rate of profit. John Hicks, who won the Nobel Prize for economics in 1972, wrote in 1935: “The best of all monopoly profits is a quiet life.” He did not mean the comment in a complimentary way. He meant that monopolies may bank their profits and slack off on trying to please their customers.
p321.zh: 垄断企业效率低下的问题往往比这些问题更深,还涉及在较长的时间内鼓励提高效率。 这里有反平衡的激励机制一方面,企业可能因为想成为垄断者并赚取高利润而争取新的发明和新的知识产权,至少在竞争赶上之前的几年内。 这样,由于对公司的竞争压力,垄断可能出现。 然而,一旦进入壁垒到位,不需要担心竞争的垄断权就只能以同样的老方式生产同样的旧产品,而与此同时,利润率仍然很高。1972年获得诺贝尔经济学奖的约翰·希克斯(John Hicks)在1935年写道 : “ 所有垄断利润中最好的是宁静的生活。 ”他并非以赞美的方式表示评论。 他的意思是,垄断者可能将利润存入银行,并放松试图取悦客户的动作。

p322.original: When AT&T provided all of the local and long-distance phone service in the United States, along with manufacturing most of the phone equipment, the payment plans and types of phones did not change much. The old joke was that you could have any color phone you wanted, as long as it was black. However, in 1982, government litigation split up AT&T into a number of local phone companies, a long-distance phone company, and a phone equipment manufacturer. An explosion of innovation followed. Services like call waiting, caller ID, three-way calling, voice mail through the phone company, mobile phones, and wireless connections to the internet all became available. Companies offered a wide range of payment plans, as well. It was no longer true that all phones were black. Instead, phones came in a wide variety of shapes and colors. The end of the telephone monopoly brought lower prices, a greater quantity of services, and also a wave of innovation aimed at attracting and pleasing customers.
p322.zh: 当AT&T在美国提供所有本地和长途电话服务,同时制造大部分电话设备时,支付计划和电话类型变化不大. 老笑话是只要是黑色的,你就可以拥有任何你想要的彩色手机. 然而,1982年,政府诉讼将AT&T拆分为多个当地电话公司,一家长途电话公司,以及一家电话设备制造商.随之而来的是一场创新的爆炸。服务如呼叫等待、呼叫者身份证、三通电话、通过电话公司发送语音邮件、移动电话、无线连接互联网等,公司也提供了广泛的付款计划。 所有电话都是黑色的已经不是事实了。 相反,电话的形状和颜色多种多样。电话垄断的结束带来了较低的价格、更多的服务以及旨在吸引和吸引客户的创新浪潮。

p324.original: In the opening case, we presented the East India Company and the Confederate States as a monopoly or near monopoly provider of a good. Nearly every American schoolchild knows the result of the “unwelcome visit” the “Mohawks” bestowed upon Boston Harbor’s tea-bearing ships—the Boston Tea Party. Regarding the cotton industry, we also know Great Britain remained neutral during the Civil War, taking neither side during the conflict.
p324.zh: 在开场白中,我们提出东印度公司和邦联国家是商品的垄断或近乎垄断的提供者.几乎每个美国学童都知道波士顿港的茶叶船(波士顿茶叶党)“莫霍克人”的“不受欢迎的访问”的结果。 关于棉花工业,我们也知道,英国在内战期间保持中立,在冲突期间既不站在一边。

p325.original: Did the monopoly nature of these business have unintended and historical consequences? Might the American Revolution have been deterred, if the East India Company had sailed the tea-bearing ships back to England? Might the southern states have made different decisions had they not been so confident “King Cotton” would force diplomatic recognition of the Confederate States of America? Of course, it is not possible to definitively answer these questions. We cannot roll back the clock and try a different scenario. We can, however, consider the monopoly nature of these businesses and the roles they played and hypothesize about what might have occurred under different circumstances.
p325.zh: 这些企业的垄断性质是否产生了意外和历史后果? 如果东印度公司将含茶船驶回英国,美国革命会不会被吓倒? 如果南方各州没有那么相信“棉花王”会迫使美国联邦国得到外交承认,那么南方各州会作出不同的决定吗? 当然,不可能确切地回答这些问题。 我们不能倒转时钟来尝试另一种情况。 然而,我们可以考虑这些企业的垄断性质,以及它们发挥的作用和对不同情况下可能发生的情况的假设。

p326.original: Perhaps if there had been legal free tea trade, the colonists would have seen things differently. There was smuggled Dutch tea in the colonial market. If the colonists had been able to freely purchase Dutch tea, they would have paid lower prices and avoided the tax.
p326.zh: 也许如果有合法的自由茶叶贸易,殖民者就会对事情有不同的见解. 在殖民市场有走私荷兰茶. 如果殖民者能够自由购买荷兰茶叶,他们本可以支付较低的价格,并避税.

p327.original: What about the cotton monopoly? With one in five jobs in Great Britain depending on Southern cotton and the Confederate States as nearly the sole provider of that cotton, why did Great Britain remain neutral during the Civil War? At the beginning of the war, Britain simply drew down massive stores of cotton. These stockpiles lasted until near the end of 1862. Why did Britain not recognize the Confederacy at that point? Two reasons: The Emancipation Proclamation and new sources of cotton. Having outlawed slavery throughout the United Kingdom in 1833, it was politically impossible for Great Britain, empty cotton warehouses or not, to recognize, diplomatically, the Confederate States. In addition, during the two years it took to draw down the stockpiles, Britain expanded cotton imports from India, Egypt, and Brazil.
p327.zh: 那棉花垄断呢?英国每五个工作岗位中就有一个依靠南方棉花和邦联国家几乎是这种棉花的唯一提供者,为什么英国在内战期间保持中立? 在战争开始时,英国只是将大量棉花的商店裁减掉. 这些储存一直持续到1862年底。英国为何不承认邦联呢? 两个原因:解放公告和棉花新来源.1833年在英国全境宣布奴隶制为非法,在政治上,大不列颠,空置的棉花仓库或不在外交上承认邦联国家是不可能的. 此外,在削减库存的两年中,英国扩大了从印度、埃及和巴西进口的棉花。

p328.original: Monopoly sellers often see no threats to their superior marketplace position. In these examples did the power of the monopoly hide other possibilities from the decision makers? Perhaps. As a result of their actions, this is how history unfolded.
p328.zh: 垄断销售商往往不会看到其优越的市场地位受到威胁。 在这些例子中,垄断的力量是否掩盖了决策者的其他可能性? 也许吧 由于他们的行动,历史就是这样发展起来的.

p330.original: A monopolist is not a price taker, because when it decides what quantity to produce, it also determines the market price. For a monopolist, total revenue is relatively low at low quantities of output, because it is not selling much. Total revenue is also relatively low at very high quantities of output, because a very high quantity will sell only at a low price. Thus, total revenue for a monopolist will start low, rise, and then decline. The marginal revenue for a monopolist from selling additional units will decline. Each additional unit a monopolist sells will push down the overall market price, and as it sells more units, this lower price applies to increasingly more units.
p330.zh: 垄断者不是价格的承受者,因为当它决定生产的数量时,它也会决定市场价格. 对于一个垄断者来说,由于产出量低,收入总额相对较低,因为它的销售量不大。收入总额在产出量非常大的情况下也相对较低,因为数量非常大只能低价出售。 因此,一个垄断集团的总收入将开始下降,上升,然后下降。垄断者出售额外单位的边际收入将减少。 每增加一个垄断商销售的单位,就会推低整个市场价格,随着其销售的单位增加,这种较低的价格适用于越来越多的单位.

p331.original: The monopolist will select the profit-maximizing level of output where MR = MC, and then charge the price for that quantity of output as determined by the market demand curve. If that price is above average cost, the monopolist earns positive profits.
p331.zh: 垄断公司将选择MR = MC的利润最大化产出水平,然后按市场需求曲线决定的这一产出数量收取价格。 如果这种价格高于平均成本,垄断者就可获得正利润。

p332.original: Monopolists are not productively efficient, because they do not produce at the minimum of the average cost curve. Monopolists are not allocatively efficient, because they do not produce at the quantity where P = MC. As a result, monopolists produce less, at a higher average cost, and charge a higher price than would a combination of firms in a perfectly competitive industry. Monopolists also may lack incentives for innovation, because they need not fear entry.
p332.zh: 垄断者效率不高,因为他们不生产平均成本曲线的最低值。垄断者不具有分配效率,因为他们生产的数量与P=MC不相同。 因此,垄断者生产的产品较少,平均成本较高,而且价格高于完全具有竞争力的行业中企业的组合。垄断者也可能缺乏创新的动力,因为他们不需要害怕进入。

p334.original: Suppose demand for a monopoly’s product falls so that its profit-maximizing price is below average variable cost. How much output should the firm supply? Hint: Draw the graph.
p334.zh: 假设对垄断产品的需求下降,使其利润最大化的价格低于平均可变成本。公司应提供多少产出?提示:画图.

p335.original: If price falls below AVC, the firm will not be able to earn enough revenues even to cover its variable costs.  In such a case, it will suffer a smaller loss if it shuts down and produces no output.  By contrast, if it stayed in operation and produced the level of output where MR = MC, it would lose all of its fixed costs plus some variable costs.  If it shuts down, it only loses its fixed costs.
p335.zh: 如果价格低于反车辆地雷,公司将无法赚取足够的收入,甚至无法支付其可变费用。 在这种情况下,如果停产而无产出,它将遭受较小的损失。与此相反,如果它继续运行并产生MR=MC的输出水平,它将损失其所有固定成本加上一些可变成本. 如果停产,只损失固定成本.

p336.original: Imagine a monopolist could charge a different price to every customer based on how much the customer is willing to pay. How would this affect monopoly profits?
p336.zh: 想象一个垄断者可以根据客户愿意支付多少,向每个客户收取不同的价格. 这将如何影响垄断利润?

p337.original: This scenario is called “perfect price discrimination.”  The result would be that the monopolist would produce more output, the same amount in fact as would be produced by a perfectly competitive industry.  However, there would be no consumer surplus since each buyer is paying exactly what they think the product is worth.  Therefore, the monopolist would be earning the maximum possible profits.
p337.zh: 这种情景被称为“完美的价格歧视 ” 。 结果,垄断者将产生更多的产出,事实上与完全有竞争力的行业生产的数量相同。 然而,不会出现消费者盈余,因为每个买方都在支付他们认为产品价值的货款。 因此,垄断者将获得最大的利润。

p339.original: How is the demand curve perceived by a perfectly competitive firm different from the demand curve perceived by a monopolist?
p339.zh: 一个完全具有竞争力的公司如何看待需求曲线,与垄断者所认为的需求曲线不同?

p340.original: How does the demand curve perceived by a monopolist compare with the market demand curve?
p340.zh: 垄断者对需求曲线的看法如何与市场需求曲线相比较?

p341.original: Is a monopolist a price taker? Explain briefly.
p341.zh: 独占者是价君吗?简单解释一下

p342.original: What is the usual shape of a total revenue curve for a monopolist? Why?
p342.zh: 独占者的收入总额曲线的通常形状是什么? 为什么?

p343.original: What is the usual shape of a marginal revenue curve for a monopolist? Why?
p343.zh: 对于独占者来说,边际收入曲线的通常形状是什么? 为什么?

p344.original: How can a monopolist identify the profit-maximizing level of output if it knows its total revenue and total cost curves?
p344.zh: 垄断者如果知道其总收入和总成本曲线,如何确定利润最大化的产出水平?

p345.original: How can a monopolist identify the profit-maximizing level of output if it knows its marginal revenue and marginal costs?
p345.zh: 垄断者如果知道其边际收入和边际成本,如何确定利润最大化的产出水平?

p346.original: When a monopolist identifies its profit-maximizing quantity of output, how does it decide what price to charge?
p346.zh: 当一个垄断者确定其利润最大化的产出数量时,它如何决定收取什么价格?

p347.original: Is a monopolist allocatively efficient? Why or why not?
p347.zh: 垄断者分配效率高吗? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p348.original: How does the quantity produced and price charged by a monopolist compare to that of a perfectly competitive firm?
p348.zh: 垄断公司生产的数量和收取的价格如何与完全具有竞争力的公司相比?

p350.original: Imagine that you are managing a small firm and thinking about entering the market of a monopolist. The monopolist is currently charging a high price, and you have calculated that you can make a nice profit charging 10% less than the monopolist. Before you go ahead and challenge the monopolist, what possibility should you consider for how the monopolist might react?
p350.zh: 想象一下,你正在管理一家小公司, 想着进入垄断者的市场。垄断者目前收取高价,你已经计算出,你可以赚到比垄断者少10%的好利润。 在你挑战垄断者之前,你应该考虑 垄断者会怎样反应?

p351.original: If a monopoly firm is earning profits, how much would you expect these profits to be diminished by entry in the long run?
p351.zh: 如果一家垄断公司在赚取利润,那么从长远来看,你期望这些利润会减少多少?

p353.original: Draw the demand curve, marginal revenue, and marginal cost curves from , and identify the quantity of output the monopoly wishes to supply and the price it will charge. Suppose demand for the monopoly’s product increases dramatically. Draw the new demand curve. What happens to the marginal revenue as a result of the increase in demand? What happens to the marginal cost curve? Identify the new profit-maximizing quantity and price. Does the answer make sense to you?
p353.zh: 绘制需求曲线、边际收入和边际成本曲线,并确定垄断部门希望供应的产出数量及其收取的价格。 如果对垄断产品的需求急剧增加的话。绘制新需求曲线 。 由于需求增加,边际收入会怎样呢?边际成本曲线会怎么样?确定新的利润最大化数量和价格。答案对你有道理吗?

p354.original: Draw a monopolist’s demand curve, marginal revenue, and marginal cost curves. Identify the monopolist’s profit-maximizing output level. Now, think about a slightly higher level of output (say Q0 + 1). According to the graph, is there any consumer willing to pay more than the marginal cost of that new level of output? If so, what does this mean?
p354.zh: 画出垄断集团的需求曲线,边际收入和边际成本曲线.识别垄断者的利润最大化输出水平 。 现在,考虑一下稍高的输出水平(如Q0+1). 根据该图,是否有任何消费者愿意支付超过这一新水平产出的边际成本? 如果是,这是什么意思?

c1.original: In this market, the demand curve intersects the long-run average cost (LRAC) curve at its downward-sloping part. A natural monopoly occurs when the quantity demanded is less than the minimum quantity it takes to be at the bottom of the long-run average cost curve.
c1.zh: 在这个市场中,需求曲线以向下倾斜的部分交叉了长期平均成本曲线(LRAC). 当所需数量低于长期平均成本曲线底部所需的最低数量时,自然垄断就会发生。

c2.original: (a) A perfectly competitive firm perceives the demand curve that it faces to be flat. The flat shape means that the firm can sell either a low quantity (Ql) or a high quantity (Qh) at exactly the same price (P). (b) A monopolist perceives the demand curve that it faces to be the same as the market demand curve, which for most goods is downward-sloping. Thus, if the monopolist chooses a high level of output (Qh), it can charge only a relatively low price (PI). Conversely, if the monopolist chooses a low level of output (Ql), it can then charge a higher price (Ph). The challenge for the monopolist is to choose the combination of price and quantity that maximizes profits.
c2.zh: (a) 完全具有竞争力的公司认为它所面临的需求曲线是平坦的。平面形状是指企业可以以完全相同的价格(P)出售低量(Ql)或高量(Qh).(b) 垄断者认为它所面临的需求曲线与市场需求曲线相同,而市场需求曲线对大多数商品来说都是向下倾斜的。 因此,如果垄断者选择高水平的产出(Qh),它只能收取相对较低的价格(PI). 相反,如果垄断者选择低水平的输出(Ql),那么它可以收取更高的价格(Ph).垄断者面临的挑战是选择价格和数量相结合,从而实现利润最大化。

c3.original: Total revenue for the monopoly firm called HealthPill first rises, then falls. Low levels of output bring in relatively little total revenue, because the quantity is low. High levels of output bring in relatively less revenue, because the high quantity pushes down the market price. The total cost curve is upward-sloping. Profits will be highest at the quantity of output where total revenue is most above total cost. The profit-maximizing level of output is not the same as the revenue-maximizing level of output, which should make sense, because profits take costs into account and revenues do not.
c3.zh: 称为"健康Pill"的垄断公司的收入总额首先上升,然后下降.产出水平低导致收入总额相对较少,因为数量少。产出水平高,收入相对较少,因为数量高,推低了市场价格。 总成本曲线向上倾斜.收益最高的是总收入最高高于总成本的产出数量。利润最大化的产出水平与收入最大化的产出水平不同,后者应该合理,因为利润考虑到了成本,收入并不合理.

c4.original: For a monopoly like HealthPill, marginal revenue decreases as it sells additional units of output. The marginal cost curve is upward-sloping. The profit-maximizing choice for the monopoly will be to produce at the quantity where marginal revenue is equal to marginal cost: that is, MR = MC. If the monopoly produces a lower quantity, then MR > MC at those levels of output, and the firm can make higher profits by expanding output. If the firm produces at a greater quantity, then MC > MR, and the firm can make higher profits by reducing its quantity of output.
c4.zh: 对于像HealthPill这样的垄断,边际收入随着销售额外的产出单位而减少.边际成本曲线向上斜.垄断的利润最大化选择是按边际收入与边际成本相等的数量生产:即MR=MC. 如果垄断生产的数量较低,那么MR > MC在这些产出水平上,公司可以通过扩大产出获得更高的利润. 如果公司生产量较大,那么MC > MR,而且公司可以通过减少产出量获得更高的利润.

c5.original: This figure begins with the same marginal revenue and marginal cost curves from the HealthPill monopoly from . It then adds an average cost curve and the demand curve that the monopolist faces. The HealthPill firm first chooses the quantity where MR = MC. In this example, the quantity is 5. The monopolist then decides what price to charge by looking at the demand curve it faces. The large box, with quantity on the horizontal axis and demand (which shows the price) on the vertical axis, shows total revenue for the firm. The lighter-shaded box, which is quantity on the horizontal axis and average cost of production on the vertical axis shows the firm's total costs. The large total revenue box minus the smaller total cost box leaves the darkly shaded box that shows total profits. Since the price charged is above average cost, the firm is earning positive profits.
c5.zh: 这一数字的起始点是相同的边际收入和来自HealthPill垄断的边际成本曲线. 然后它又增加了平均成本曲线和垄断者面临的需求曲线.健康药剂公司首先选择MR=MC的数量。 在这个例子中,数量是5。 然后,垄断者通过查看其面临的需求曲线来决定收取的价格。 大箱在水平轴上数量和需求(显示价格)在垂直轴上,显示公司总收入.较轻的阴影箱,是水平轴上的数量和垂直轴上的平均生产成本,显示了公司的总成本.庞大的总收入框减去较小的总成本框,留下了显示总利润的暗黑阴影框. 由于收取的价格高于平均成本,公司正在赚取正利润。

c6.original:
In Step 1, the monopoly chooses the profit-maximizing level of output Q1, by choosing the quantity where MR = MC. In Step 2, the monopoly decides how much to charge for output level Q1 by drawing a line straight up from Q1 to point R on its perceived demand curve. Thus,
the monopoly will charge a price (P1). In Step 3, the monopoly identifies its profit. Total revenue will be Q1 multiplied by P1. Total cost will be 
Q1 multiplied by the average cost of producing Q1, which point S shows on the average cost curve to be P2. Profits will be the total revenue rectangle minus the total cost rectangle, which the shaded zone in the figure shows.
c6.zh: 在步骤1中,垄断通过选择MR=MC的量来选择输出Q1的利润最大化水平. 在第2步中,垄断通过从Q1直接绘制一条线,将R指向其感知的需求曲线来决定输出级别Q1的收费金额. 因此,垄断将收取价格(P1)。 在第三步中,垄断确定了利润。总收入为问题1乘以P1。 总成本为Q1乘以生成Q1的平均成本,S点显示平均成本曲线为P2.利润将是总收入矩减去总成本矩,图中的阴影区显示了这一点。

c7.original: Because the market demand curve is conditional, the marginal revenue curve for a monopolist lies beneath the demand curve.
c7.zh: 由于市场需求曲线是有条件的,所以垄断者的边际收入曲线位于需求曲线下方.
